description:
FILED s446l (agent L) while probing #525; PRE-EXISTING.

REPRO (perl vs ./runpcl), three lines:
  no strict 'refs';
  our $tag = "M";
  print "01 [${\"tag\"}]\n";
perl prints `01 [M]`.  PCL emits
    (p-cast-$ (p-backslash "tag\"}))
-- an unterminated CL string -- and SBCL dies with `read error during load:
end of file`, so NOTHING in the file runs, not one line before or after.
Same severity class as #419 (one bad literal costs the whole program).

CAUSE (diagnosed, not fixed): inside a double-quoted string `\"` is an
ESCAPED QUOTE, so the block's content is `"tag"` and the construct is the
symbolic deref ${"tag"}.  The interpolation path re-parses the block body
WITHOUT first undoing the string's own escapes, so it sees a backslash
followed by a bareword-ish `"tag"` and reads it as perl's REFERENCE operator
-- hence `p-backslash` -- and then the un-unescaped `\"` walks into the
emitted CL string literal.  The likely site is Pl/PExpr/StringInterpolation.pm
(the `${ â¦ }` block arm) or the fragment re-parse it hands the body to
(Pl::Parser::fragment_doc, #435's family).

Note the CODE spelling is different and already right: `${\"tag\"}` outside
a string IS perl's ref-then-deref of a constant, and `${"tag"}` in code is
the symbolic deref -- both work.  It is only the IN-STRING spelling that
conflates them.

BAR: the repro + `"@{\"name\"}"` + a name built from a variable +
`"${\\$ref}"` (a real hard ref in a string, which must stay a deref) + the
two CODE spellings unchanged; an unreadable-CL guard (the emitted file must
READ, which is the cheap gate here -- sbcl --script tools/check-parens.lisp on
the output, or a load).
subject: An interpolated symbolic deref `"${\"name\"}"` emits an UNTERMINATED CL string -- the WHOLE FILE fails to read (#419 class, total loss)
